statement_record.book: For sets A, B, C write C^B for the set of all functions B -> C. Currying f : A x B -> C gives the unique f~ : A -> C^B with f~(a)(b) = f(a,b), and every phi : A -> C^B arises this way, so Sets(A x B, C) = Sets(A, C^B). The bijection is mediated by eval : C^B x B -> C, eval(g,b) = g(b), which is universal: for each f : A x B -> C there is a unique f~ with eval . (f~ x 1_B) = f (equation 6.1).

evidence.intree_statement: Program Definition InternalHomFunctor `(C : Category) {E : @Cartesian C} {O : @Closed C _} : C^op ∏ C ⟶ C := {| fobj := fun p => @exponent_obj C E O (fst p) (snd p);   (* (a, b) ↦ b ^ a *)  fmap := fun x y '(f, g) => curry (g ∘ eval ∘ second (op f)) |}.
[f, g] := curry (g ∘ eval ∘ second f) : b ^ a ~> b' ^ a', which pre-composes by f in the exponent and post-composes by g in the base.

(* Functoriality of the partial functor F(w, -) in the second variable. *) Lemma bimap_comp_id_left {F : C ∏ D ⟶ E} {w} `(f : y ~{D}~> z) `(g : x ~{D}~> y) : bimap (id[w]) (f ∘ g) ≈ bimap id f ∘ bimap id g.
Lemma bimap_id_id {F : C ∏ D ⟶ E} {x y} : bimap (id[x]) (id[y]) ≈ id.
Theorem second_id {x y : C} : second (id[y]) ≈ id[x × y].

statement_record.book: In a CCC, exponentiation by a fixed A is a functor (-)^A : C -> C: on objects B |-> B^A, on beta : B -> C the arrow beta^A := (beta . eps)~ : B^A -> C^A, the unique map with eps . (beta^A x 1_A) = beta . eps. The functor laws (1_B)^A = 1_{B^A} and (gamma . beta)^A = gamma^A . beta^A are proved.
statement_record.intree: InternalHomFunctor : C^op ∏ C ⟶ C with fobj (a,b) = b^a and fmap (f,g) = curry (g ∘ eval ∘ second (op f)); at f := id this is curry (g ∘ eval ∘ second id) ≈ curry (g ∘ eval) = g^a (second_id, Structure/Cartesian.v:340). The two functor laws in the fixed-first-argument variable are the generic bifunctor lemmas at F := InternalHomFunctor: bimap_id_id (bimap id id ≈ id, i.e. (1_B)^A = 1_{B^A}) and bimap_comp_id_left, whose in-file comment is literally 'Functoriality of the partial functor F(w, -) in the second variable' (bimap id (f ∘ g) ≈ bimap id f ∘ bimap id g, i.e. (gamma ∘ beta)^A = gamma^A ∘ beta^A).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger: the library proves functoriality in BOTH variables at once (a bifunctor C^op ∏ C ⟶ C, contravariant in the exponent as well), whose restriction along {A} × C is exactly Awodey's (-)^A, with his beta^A := (beta ∘ eps)~ recovered on the nose modulo second_id. One packaging caveat, recorded for honesty: no OBJECT of type `C ⟶ C` for fixed A is constructed — the library has no generic 'fix one argument of a bifunctor' combinator (Functor/Hom.v:60 Curried_Hom does this only for the external hom; the `Curry` used in the Structure/Closed.v:189 notation lives inside a commented-out stub and is not defined anywhere). The mathematical content of Prop 6.6 — the action on arrows and both functor laws — is nevertheless fully available as instances of the above.

evidence.intree_statement: Theorem curry_id {x y z : C} (f : x ~> y) : curry (@id _ (y × z)) ∘ f ≈ curry (first f).
Corollary curry_comp {x y z w : C} (f : z ~> w) (g : x × y ~> z) : curry (f ∘ g) ≈ curry (f ∘ eval) ∘ curry g.
Corollary curry_comp_l {x y z w : C} (f : y × z ~> w) (g : x ~> y) : curry f ∘ g ≈ curry (f ∘ first g).
natural in x, y and z, expressing (- × y) ⊣ (- ^ y). Currying is the left-to-right direction, uncurrying its inverse, and eval is the image of the identity on z^y (the counit of the adjunction).

statement_record.book: eta := (1_{A x B})~ : A -> (A x B)^B is the transpose of the identity (in Sets, eta(a)(b) = (a,b)); it is the unit of the product/exponential adjunction, and for f : Z x A -> B the transpose can be computed from the exponentiation functor as f~ = f^A . eta, with eta : Z -> (Z x A)^A and f^A : (Z x A)^A -> B^A.
statement_record.intree: The arrow itself occurs only as the anonymous term `curry (@id _ (y × z))` inside Theorem curry_id (line 201), which states its naturality-in-the-source form curry (id[y × z]) ∘ f ≈ curry (first f). The book's computation rule is the g := id instance of Corollary curry_comp (line 177): curry (f ∘ g) ≈ curry (f ∘ eval) ∘ curry g at g := id[x × y] and z := x × y gives, after id_right, curry f ≈ curry (f ∘ eval) ∘ curry id — exactly f~ = f^A ∘ eta.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger on the equation (curry_comp is the general two-arrow substitution law, of which the book's f~ = f^A ∘ eta is the g := id special case), but intree-weaker on the packaging: eta is never named, defined, or identified as an adjunction unit. Contrast the counit, which IS a named in-tree definition (eval := uncurry id, line 75).
